name: Tad
label: Sub Pop
lede: A former butcher from Idaho, a bassist from a logging town, a van across Europe with Nirvana, and some of the heaviest records Seattle ever made.

eras.title: Total Audio Destruction
eras.text: Tad Doyle had been a drummer in the Seattle band H-Hour and a butcher by trade. He started Tad alone, playing every instrument on a demo, and Sub Pop's Bruce Pavitt and Jonathan Poneman saw a frontman they could build a legend around.

years.h: Tad Doyle records a demo alone and Sub Pop names the band after him
years.p: Tad Doyle plays every instrument on a three-song demo. He wanted the band called Total Audio Destruction; Pavitt and Poneman insisted on Tad.
years.xp: Doyle told Vice he honestly didn't want the band named after him at first. Sub Pop won, and the name became part of the myth.

years.h: Kurt Danielson, Steve Wied and Gary Thorstensen fill out Tad
years.p: Bassist [[Kurt Danielson|22f1202f-1ab5-41c3-8bc8-bd1d20bbe18b]] (ex-[[Bundle of Hiss|aaa673a8-af81-4140-8cb8-800406c1eace]]), drummer Steve Wied (ex-[[Skin Yard|0119843b-4d56-47b6-ac0d-11528259bf0a]]) and guitarist Gary Thorstensen join, and Doyle moves to guitar and vocals.

years.h: Daisy / Ritual Device: Tad's first single
years.p: Tad's debut 7-inch comes out on Sub Pop, produced by [[Jack Endino|d06cca33-9167-4049-b5ce-6a6aeff60a8d]].

eras.title: Sub Pop's backwoods myth goes to Europe
eras.text: Sub Pop sold Tad as a butcher and a lumberjack straight out of the woods, and the band played along. In late 1989 they crammed into one van with Nirvana for six weeks in Europe and came back with a record produced by Steve Albini.

years.h: God's Balls: Tad's debut album
years.p: Tad's first full-length comes out on Sub Pop early in 1989, again produced by Jack Endino.

q: They liked to kick it up and make it more fantastic than life.
years.h: Sub Pop blows up Tad Doyle's butcher past into a legend
years.p: Pavitt and Poneman push a backwoods, blue-collar image: Tad Doyle the Idaho butcher, Kurt Danielson from a logging town. Doyle says it was all true, just made bigger than life.

years.h: Lamefest: Tad share the Moore Theatre with [[Mudhoney|e675295a-1efe-4247-aa3b-53b78d0cdffc]] and Nirvana
years.p: Sub Pop's Lamefest puts Tad, Mudhoney and Nirvana on one bill at Seattle's Moore Theatre, the night Bruce Pavitt called the scene's turning point.

yt: 5 facts from Nirvana's 1989 European tour with Tad
years.h: Tad and Nirvana share one van for 37 shows in 42 days
years.p: The Heavier Than Heaven tour starts in Newcastle: Tad and [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] in a single small van across Europe, mostly sleeping on floors. In Rome, Kurt Danielson shouts an insult at the Pope near the Vatican.
years.xp: The tour ran 37 shows in 42 days. [[Krist Novoselic|ac05e29f-0561-4445-bb26-5562d2389531]] got the band thrown out of an Amsterdam hotel, and on the same Rome night, November 27, [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] smashed his guitar and climbed a speaker stack.

years.h: Lamefest UK at the London Astoria closes the tour
years.p: Tad play between Nirvana and headliners Mudhoney at the Astoria on Charing Cross Road, Sub Pop's big showcase for the British press.

years.h: Salt Lick, recorded by [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]
years.p: Tad's EP is recorded by Steve Albini; the CD version grows to nine tracks.
years.xp: MTV rejected the video for Wood Goblins, deeming the band too ugly for the channel, according to Vice.

eras.title: Sued by Pepsi, sued by a stranger
eras.text: Tad's best-known album came with the band's worst luck. Butch Vig produced it, and then both its cover and its single brought lawsuits that forced Sub Pop to change the art.

years.h: 8-Way Santa, produced by [[Butch Vig|ba30915c-4d33-43c5-8c37-ead0b8061517]]
years.p: Tad's second album, made with Butch Vig, the producer of [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]]'s Nevermind. Its singles are Jinx and Jack Pepsi.

q: We were magnets for ridiculousness, I guess.
years.h: Pepsi sues Tad over Jack Pepsi, and a couple sues over the cover
years.p: The Jack Pepsi single sleeve reworks the Pepsi logo to read Tad, and Pepsi sues. Then a woman pictured on the 8-Way Santa cover sees it in Spin and sues too.
years.xp:
The cover was a 1960s thrift-store snapshot of a man fondling a woman's breast. According to Wikipedia, one of the pair had since become a born-again Christian. Sub Pop pulled it and put a band photo on the cover instead.

Doyle told Vice the Pepsi call came from a disgruntled former Sub Pop employee, and that the band saw the logo swap as a harmless joke.

years.h: Steve Wied quits; [[Rey Washam|33b09380-db28-4c9c-9fdd-ab5c20049c61]] fills in on drums
years.p: Drummer Steve Wied leaves under the label and business strain. Rey Washam, formerly of [[Scratch Acid|75687111-1585-4df2-83e6-ce52e7fa2bb0]], covers for a short time.
years.xp: Doyle told Vice he might have overstepped his authority with Wied. Wied went on to Willard and Foil.

eras.title: Two majors, two firings
eras.text: A cameo in Cameron Crowe's Singles got Tad a deal with Warner-owned Giant, and a record produced by J Mascis. Giant dropped them over a poster the band says it had nothing to do with; East West dropped them two weeks into their next album.

years.h: Josh Sinder, ex-[[The Accüsed|36bcdf2f-f481-4669-a0fd-23049377cbab]], joins on drums
years.p: Josh Sinder debuts on the Salem / Leper single, Tad's last Sub Pop release.

years.h: Tad appear in Singles and sign to Giant Records
years.p: Tad's cameo in Cameron Crowe's grunge romance Singles is followed by a deal with Giant, a Warner Music label.

years.h: Inhaler, produced by [[J Mascis|82315599-2215-4c3e-a36f-87be58d06ec0]]
years.p: Tad's major-label debut is recorded at Studio D in Sausalito with [[Dinosaur Jr.|77c167d2-4965-4421-830a-9815e4956475]]'s J Mascis. Reviews are good, sales are not; the only single is Leafy Incline.

years.cap: The poster that got Tad dropped
years.h: A Bill Clinton pot poster gets Tad dropped by Giant
years.p: On [[Soundgarden|153c9281-268f-4cf3-8938-f5a4593e5df4]]'s Superunknown tour, a promo poster shows Bill Clinton smoking a joint under a drug-pun slogan. Giant blames the band and drops them.
years.xp: Doyle told Vice the poster came from the label's art department and the band had nothing to do with it, but Giant used it as the reason to cut them. The Soundgarden tour itself did little for Tad's sales.

years.h: Live Alien Broadcasts on Futurist
years.p: A best-of cut live in the studio, released on the small Futurist label.

years.h: Infrared Riding Hood: dropped two weeks after release
years.p: With Gary Thorstensen gone, Tad Doyle and Jack Endino play all the guitars. Two weeks after East West/Elektra releases it, the band's A&R rep is fired and all her acts are dropped.
years.xp: The rep also looked after [[Clutch|0cdb0359-5698-487d-9aae-a25fb4dcdc4d]]. Doyle told Vice the label barely knew who Tad were by then.

eras.title: Running out of road
eras.text: Tad kept going without a big label, with a new drummer and a few final singles. Tad Doyle was struggling with drugs and alcohol, and in 1999, eleven years in, the band stopped.

years.h: Josh Sinder leaves; Foil's Mike Mongrain takes over drums
years.p: Josh Sinder quits to form the Hot Rod Lunatics. Mike Mongrain, who played in Foil with former Tad drummer Steve Wied, replaces him.

years.h: Oppenheimer's Pretty Nightmare: Tad's last single
years.p: Tad's final release, backed with Accident on the Way to Church, comes out on Seattle's Up Records.

years.h: Tad break up after eleven years
years.p: Tad split in 1999. Doyle told Vice he was fighting drug and alcohol addiction in the band's late years; he has been sober for years since.

eras.title: Doom, a documentary and a victory lap
eras.text: Tad Doyle went heavier and slower, first in Hog Molly and later in the doom band Brothers of the Sonic Cloth, and ran his own studio. A documentary and a set of Sub Pop reissues brought Tad's records back into print.

years.h: Tad Doyle forms Hog Molly
years.p: Doyle starts Hog Molly with Willard bassist Ty Garcia and 50 Paces guitarist Martin Chandler; they release Kung-Fu Cocktail Grip.

yt: TAD: Busted Circuits and Ringing Ears documentary
years.h: Busted Circuits and Ringing Ears: the Tad documentary
years.p: A feature documentary tells Tad's story, lawsuits and all, with the band and their Seattle peers including [[Mark Arm|3f99d2df-8859-4249-8a70-84fe04c5a096]].

years.h: Kurt Danielson comes home from France to write a novel
years.p: Kurt Danielson, who had moved to France after Tad, returns to Seattle and later plays in Misericords with ex-Tad drummer Mike Mongrain.

years.h: Tad Doyle and Gary Thorstensen play Sub Pop's 25th anniversary
years.p: At Sub Pop's 25th birthday show, Doyle and Thorstensen reunite to play songs from Tad's first three records.

years.h: Sub Pop reissues God's Balls, Salt Lick and 8-Way Santa
years.p: Jack Endino remasters Tad's three Sub Pop albums for deluxe reissues. Doyle, now in the doom band Brothers of the Sonic Cloth with his wife Peggy and running Witch Ape Studio, tells Vice the band's legacy is its integrity.

years.h: Quick and Dirty: lost 1995–99 recordings
years.p: A vinyl-only Record Store Day release collects unreleased Tad songs from 1995–1999 and some live tracks.

sources.title: Vice: Magnets for Ridiculousness: The Story of TAD
